mainProgression.description: The quintessential Australian narrative progression. Paul Kelly uses the circular I-V-vi-IV movement to depict the protagonist's long physical and emotional journey from Queensland down to Sydney.

harmonicFunction: G (I) - Tonic chord giving the song its home base and narrative resolution
D (V) - Dominant chord propelling the physical journey down the highway
Em (vi) - Relative minor introducing regret and emotional reflection
C (IV) - Subdominant chord adding hope and emotional lift

techniques.name: Syncopated Driving Acoustic Strum
techniques.description: An energetic, driving 4/4 down-up acoustic strumming pattern with a buoyant backbeat accent that keeps long storytelling verses exciting

notes: Accented downstrokes on beats 2 and 4 (matching the snare pulse)
Constant right-hand forearm motion swinging from the wrist
sequence: Beat 1: Solid downstroke on the root bass string
Beat 2: Accented strum across all strings
Beat &: Light upstroke brushing top 3 strings
Beat 4: Crisp accented downstroke, followed by quick upstroke on the &
tips: Keep the right arm relaxed and moving in perpetual 8th-note motion
Do not dig the pick too deeply into the strings — skim the surface with a flexible pick
Tapping your foot on beats 1 and 3 helps anchor the driving pulse

techniques.name: Rapid Open Cowboy Chord Turnaround
techniques.description: Clean, rapid switching between open G, D, Em, and C chords at 108 BPM with zero dropped beats

notes: Use the 4-finger G chord (3-2-0-0-3-3) to keep ring and pinky fingers anchored on strings 1 and 2
Keep the 3rd fret on string 2 anchored when moving to Cadd9 or standard C
Pivot your index and middle fingers swiftly to form the D chord
sequence: Switch cleanly to D for 2 beats
Finish the phrase on C for 2 beats before resolving to G - D - G
tips: Anchoring fingers on the high B and E strings eliminates fumble time during changes
Focus on landing the bass note of the new chord precisely on beat 1
Practice the G - D - G turnaround in isolation until it is second nature

sections.name: Intro
sections.description: Paul Kelly establishes the infectious 108 BPM acoustic groove with a clean cycle through the signature G - D - Em - C progression.
sections.progression: G - D - Em - C - G - D - G
notes: Count in at 108 BPM with driving folk-rock enthusiasm
Anchor your strumming on the low G bass note
Execute the crisp G - D - G turnaround to conclude the intro
sections.exerciseLabel: Paul Kelly Driving Acoustic Folk Intro

sections.name: Verse
sections.description: The storytelling verse unfolds over the circular I-V-vi-IV progression, carrying the narrative across the highway.
sections.progression: G - D - Em - C - G - D - G
notes: Keep the rhythm punchy and supportive behind the lyrics
Let the open strings ring out without muddying
Lock in with the 2 and 4 accents

sections.name: Chorus
sections.description: The chorus hook pushes forward on the dominant D chord, opening up for the memorable sing-along hook.
notes: Deliver the D chord with extra dynamic projection
Move into G and C with fluid down-up strums
Build tension before diving into the next verse

sections.name: Scale Practice Exercise
sections.description: Two-octave open G major scale run demonstrating the diatonic foundation of the vocal melody and acoustic transitions.
notes: Alternate picking across all 6 strings in open position
Connect scale tones directly to the G and Em chord shapes
Maintain clean articulation with a metronome
sections.exerciseLabel: Open G Major Australian Folk Scale

beginner.title: Master the G, D, Em, C Open Chords
steps: Learn open G, D, Em, and C chord shapes
Practice transitioning between G and D without hesitation
Work on the full verse sequence (G - D - Em - C - G - D - G) at 80 BPM
Strum simple downstrokes on each beat to memorize the narrative progression

intermediate.title: Develop the Driving 108 BPM Rhythm
steps: Incorporate the syncopated down-up strumming pattern with accents on 2 and 4
Speed up smoothly to the full recording tempo of 108 BPM
Practice switching into the chorus progression (D - G - C - D) seamlessly
Play through the entire 3-minute song structure without stopping

advanced.title: Vocal Accompaniment & Australian Campfire Performance
steps: Sing lead vocals while maintaining the driving acoustic rhythm
Add subtle bass note walkups between chord changes
Incorporate light percussive palm chucks on the backbeat
Deliver the full narrative arc with dynamic acoustic conviction

commonMistakes: Dragging the tempo during the storytelling verses — keep the rhythm driving at 108 BPM
Stumbling on the quick G - D - G turnaround at the end of each verse line
Strumming too aggressively on the D chord and hitting unwanted low bass strings
Losing the backbeat groove by playing unaccented straight strums
practiceRoutine: 2 minutes: Open chord finger warm-up across G, D, Em, and C
5 minutes: Isolated drill of the G - D - Em - C verse turnaround at 95 BPM
5 minutes: Full verse progression at 108 BPM with driving down-up rhythm
5 minutes: Chorus flow (D - G - C - D) practicing dynamic vocal support
5 minutes: Complete song play-through focusing on storytelling rhythm
focusAreas: Clean chord changes between G, D, Em, and C
metronomeWork: Set metronome to 90 BPM to practice the verse progression chord shifts
Increase by 4 BPM intervals up to the full 108 BPM recording tempo
Practice with clicks on beats 2 and 4 to internalize the folk-rock pocket
Record your practice to check that your rhythm remains solid during chord transitions
